title: Design System: Golmuri Janch Ghar — Patient Portal

page-title.purpose: The centred title in BandBar; 16.5px rising to 18px at sm.

section.purpose: SectionHead, above a group of cards.

field.purpose: Every input. 16px is the iOS zoom threshold, not a preference.

value.purpose: The answer half of a Fact pair.

body.purpose: Notes and explanatory copy, relaxed leading.

caption.purpose: Hints under a field, tag text.

eyebrow.purpose: The uppercase label half of a Fact pair.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Every card, day mode. Tinted with the canvas hue. Night mode redefines it in black at far higher alpha.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Popovers and menus. Nearly useless alone in night mode, which is why --elev-pop also steps lighter.

shadows.name: band
shadows.purpose: Under the teal band. Black rather than slate: a slate tint was lighter than the night canvas and read as a halo.

shadows.name: bezel
shadows.purpose: A top highlight on glass tiles, not a drop shadow.

motion.name: out-fluid
motion.purpose: The single curve across press, entry, popover and page transition.

motion.name: tap
motion.purpose: Press feedback on every tappable surface. 160ms is under the threshold where a press feels reported rather than felt.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: Page entry choreography; nothing blocks interaction while it plays.

motion.name: page-in
motion.purpose: Declared in template.tsx so it replays on every navigation. Opacity only because .rise already owns the travel.

motion.name: skeleton
motion.purpose: A breath rather than a sweeping shimmer — a sweep repaints every frame for every block on screen.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Teal fill, generous 20px radius, sized for a thumb. Presses to 0.975.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:0.5rem; border:none; border-radius:20px; padding:0.875rem 1.25rem; font-size:14.5px; font-weight:600; background:#3a7788; color:#ffffff; cursor:pointer; box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgb(16 40 50 / 0.04), 0 10px 26px -14px rgb(16 40 50 / 0.16); user-select:none; transition:background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1), transform 160ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#2a5f6f; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #3a7788; outline-offset:2px; border-radius:8px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:scale(0.975); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The content surface. 26px radius, hairline, canvas-tinted shadow. Padding belongs to the caller.
components.html:
Your reports

Two reports are ready to view.
components.css: .ds-card { background:#ffffff; border:1px solid #e2e9ed; border-radius:26px; box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgb(16 40 50 / 0.04), 0 10px 26px -14px rgb(16 40 50 / 0.16); } .ds-card-pad { padding:1rem 1.25rem 1.25rem; } .ds-section { margin:0 0 0.5rem; font-size:17px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:-0.012em; color:#12262f; } .ds-body { margin:0; font-size:13px; line-height:1.625; color:#4a626d; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Recessed fill that lifts to card white on focus. 16px text is a functional threshold — below it iOS Safari zooms the page and does not zoom back.
components.css: .ds-field { display:block; width:100%; } .ds-field-label { display:block; margin-bottom:0.5rem; font-size:13px; font-weight:600; color:#4a626d; } .ds-input { display:block; width:100%; border-radius:20px; border:1px solid #e2e9ed; background:#f4f7f9; padding:0.875rem 1rem; font-size:16px; color:#12262f; transition:border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1), background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1), box-shadow 200ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color:#5d6e78; } .ds-input:focus { outline:none; border-color:#3a7788; background:#ffffff; box-shadow:0 0 0 4px rgb(58 119 136 / 0.1); } .ds-hint { display:block; margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:12px; line-height:1.625; color:#5d6e78; }

components.name: Icon Chip
components.description: Circular pale plate behind a hairline icon. Four tones: brand, ok, notice, alert.
components.css: .ds-chip { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:2.75rem; width:2.75rem; border-radius:9999px; flex-shrink:0; } .ds-chip-brand { background:#e6f0f3; color:#3a7788; } .ds-chip-ok { background:#ddf1e8; color:#157a4e; } .ds-chip-notice { background:#fbf0da; color:#8a5a10; } .ds-chip-alert { background:#fce8e6; color:#ba3737; }

components.name: Tag
components.description: Small state capsule. Same four tones plus neutral.
components.html: Paid Awaiting approval Fasting
components.css: .ds-tag { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:0.375rem; border-radius:9999px; padding:0.25rem 0.75rem; font-size:12px; font-weight:500; } .ds-tag-neutral { background:#f4f7f9; color:#4a626d; } .ds-tag-ok { background:#ddf1e8; color:#157a4e; } .ds-tag-notice { background:#fbf0da; color:#8a5a10; } .ds-tag-alert { background:#fce8e6; color:#ba3737; }

components.name: Note
components.description: A low-stakes explanation. The tint carries the tone; the text stays soft so the panel never shouts.
components.html: Scan this code with any UPI app. Tap “Already paid?” once the payment goes through.
components.css: .ds-note { display:flex; gap:0.75rem; border-radius:20px; padding:0.875rem 1rem; background:#e6f0f3; color:#4a626d; } .ds-note-icon { margin-top:1px; flex-shrink:0; color:#3a7788; } .ds-note-body { font-size:13px; line-height:1.625; }

components.name: Fact
components.description: The portal's standard label/value pair — uppercase eyebrow over a semibold value.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-facts { display:flex; gap:2rem; } .ds-fact-label { margin:0; font-size:11.5px; font-weight:500; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:0.08em; color:#5d6e78; } .ds-fact-value { margin:0.25rem 0 0; font-size:14.5px; font-weight:600; color:#12262f; } .num { font-feature-settings:"tnum" 1, "lnum" 1; }

components.name: Band
components.description: The deep-teal header every page opens with — two radial gradients, a 32px bottom curve, and the white pill that is the only fully-round button.
components.html:
Your reports

components.css: .ds-band { background-color:#2a5f6f; background-image:radial-gradient(120% 90% at 88% -10%, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.14), transparent 58%), radial-gradient(90% 70% at 4% 108%, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.16), transparent 60%); color:#ffffff; border-radius:0 0 32px 32px; padding:1.25rem 1.25rem 2rem; box-shadow:0 16px 34px -22px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5); } .ds-band-bar { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:0.75rem; } .ds-band-title { margin:0; font-size:18px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-0.012em; color:#ffffff; } .ds-btn-on-band { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; border-radius:9999px; background:#ffffff; padding:0.5rem 1rem; font-size:13.5px; font-weight:600; color:#2a5f6f; text-decoration:none; } .ds-btn-on-band:hover { background:rgb(255 255 255 / 0.9); }

narrative.overview:
Almost everyone who opens this portal is waiting to find out something about their own body. That single fact sets the temperature of the whole surface. The deep-teal band a page opens with, the three wave layers drifting along its foot at seventeen to thirty-one seconds a cycle, the slow opacity breath of a skeleton instead of a glinting shimmer — none of it is decoration for its own sake. It is a room that refuses to feel urgent while someone waits in it.

The portal is built from four surfaces and nothing else: the full-bleed teal band every page opens with, the white card that carries content, the recessed surface strip inside a card, and the pale-teal chip. Keeping that vocabulary this short is what makes twelve screens read as one product rather than twelve pages. Depth is a genuine ramp — canvas, surface, card, popover — and a floating menu separates from the card beneath it by taking its own step, never by borrowing the card's fill.

It is also the only surface in this system with a real night mode, and the two themes are not a colour inversion. They disagree about what "darker" means, so shadows, hover directions and the brand's foreground all get redefined rather than flipped: in day mode a button hover goes deeper, in night mode it goes lighter, because night mode's button ink is near-black. Every one of those inversions is a separate deliberate decision, and the reasoning is written into globals.css beside the tokens.
keyCharacteristics: Four surfaces only — band, card, recessed strip, chip — across every screen
Full day/night theming through rgb() triplet tokens with <alpha-value> support, not a filter
A generous radius scale topping out at a 32px band curve; nothing here is sharp
One easing curve (cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)) across press, entry, popover and page transition
Touch-first by construction: 44px minimum hit areas, 16px fields, dvh heights
Motion is choreographed then fully surrendered under prefers-reduced-motion

rules.name: The Four Surfaces Rule
rules.body: Band, card, recessed strip, chip. A new screen composes from those four; it does not invent a fifth. This is the single reason the portal reads as one product across twelve screens.

rules.name: The Elevation-Step Rule
rules.body: A floating panel takes its own step on the ramp (--elev-pop, --line-pop, .popover). A popover drawn with the card recipe is made of exactly the fill and hairline of the card it covers, and the two merge into one slab.

rules.name: The Two-Themes-Disagree Rule
rules.body: Never derive night mode by inverting day mode. Shadows go black rather than slate because the night canvas is darker than the day shadow's tint; hover moves lighter rather than deeper because the button's ink is near-black. Each pair is defined independently in globals.css.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: Any input, select or textarea computes to at least 16px. Below that, Safari on iOS zooms the whole page in on focus and does not zoom back out — the patient is left pinching their way back to a legible layout, once per field, and the booking form has nine of them.

rules.name: The Tabular Numeral Rule
rules.body: Anything numeric that sits in a column — amounts, results, dates in a list — carries .num (tnum, lnum). Proportional digits make a column of prices jitter.

rules.name: The Darker-Than-What-It-Falls-On Rule
rules.body: Any new shadow must be darker than the surface beneath it in both themes, or it will read as a halo in one of them. Black is the safe answer; slate is not.

dos: Do compose from the four surfaces — band, card, recessed strip, chip.
Do give any floating panel its own elevation step (--elev-pop, --line-pop, .popover), never the card recipe.
Do put every input through inputCls, or give it a size of at least 16px of its own.
Do wrap small controls in .hit so a finger gets 44px even where the eye sees less.
Do define day and night values independently, with the reason in a comment beside them.
Do add .num to numerals that sit in a column.
Do give every new animation a prefers-reduced-motion answer that keeps the fade and drops the travel.
Do use overscroll-behavior on anything that scrolls inside the page.
donts: Don't use backdrop-filter for the glass tiles. They sit on a flat canvas, so blurring returns the same flat colour — and thirteen live blurs in a scroll container is the one thing that reliably wrecks the mid-range Android that is most of this lab's traffic.
Don't tint a shadow with slate. It is lighter than the night canvas and becomes a halo.
Don't invert a day token to get its night value.
Don't let a field compute below 16px.
Don't put a hover-only affordance on a touch target without a (hover: hover) guard — a tap fires :hover and leaves the card stuck raised.
Don't add a fifth surface or a sharp corner.
